title: security: enforce RBAC v2 KMS region residency + audit logging for private deployments
author: Ayesha Patel
description:
Context: Customers on Private deployments require strict data residency guarantees for KMS-managed keys and full audit trails of key usage. ENG-4217 and SEC-113 capture the product and compliance requirements.

Motivation: Enforce RBAC v2 policies that prevent creation or use of KMS key references outside an allowed region residency set for a given account/org. Add end-to-end audit logging for KMS operations (encrypt/decrypt/sign) surfaced to the control plane audit stream and optional push to customer sidecar (for Private installs). This reduces accidental cross-region key references and enables forensic trails for regulated customers.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds RBAC v2 policy predicates and a policy bundle that ties KMS key residency constraints to organizational settings.
- Implements an admission-time validation hook in the Private control plane that rejects resources (secrets, key references, deployment configs) referencing KMS keys outside allowed regions.
- Enhances KMS integration to emit structured audit events for key operations; events are persisted to control-plane audit-log and optionally forwarded to customer audit sinks in Private installs.
- Migration path: validation first runs in audit mode (warnings only) for 2 weeks, then enforcement is enabled via feature flag and rolled out to Dedicated/Private clusters in canary waves.
- Docs and infra: updates to redwood-private-installer to populate residency config and to RBAC policy bundle docs.

Checklist: [x] RBAC policy predicates + bundle
[x] Admission webhook and server-side validation
[x] KMS audit event schema + persistence
[x] Migration job to detect non-compliant resources
[x] Tests (unit/integration) + e2e validation on staging
[x] Docs and release notes

Testing and rollout plan: Start with audit-only mode on staging and 1 small customer canary (opt-in). Collect warnings and run migration script to list/categorize violating resources. After 14 days, flip enforcement for canary orgs, then expand to remaining Private installs. Rollback plan: revert enforcement flag and process queued warnings; migration script can auto-remediate when keys are available in-residency.

Risks and mitigations: Admission webhook adds a small latency (~5-10ms) to resource writes - we benchmarked and it's within SLO. Migration may surface significant violations for large orgs; we provide tooling to bulk-update key references or request region-mirrored keys.

Related: linear/ENG-4217, SEC-113, SUP-2984.
